scenes.tts: Each summer, part of the deep water in the Chesapeake Bay runs very low on oxygen. Fish and crabs swim away from it. Animals that cannot leave may get sick or die. People call this low-oxygen water a dead zone. How can too much fertilizer make part of the Bay run out of oxygen?

scenes.narration: Each summer, part of the deep water in the Chesapeake Bay runs very low on oxygen. Fish and crabs swim away from it. Animals that cannot leave may get sick or die. People call this low-oxygen water a dead zone. How can too much fertilizer make part of the Bay run out of oxygen?

scenes.tts: A nutrient is a substance living things need to grow. Algae are tiny living things that grow in water. They need nitrogen and phosphorus. Farm fertilizer and manure contain these nutrients. So does wastewater. Rain washes nutrients from fields and lawns into rivers.
scenes.visual: nutrient chips wash from the field into the Bay
scenes.narration: A nutrient is a substance living things need to grow. Algae are tiny living things that grow in water. They need nitrogen and phosphorus. Farm fertilizer and manure contain these nutrients. So does wastewater. Rain washes nutrients from fields and lawns into rivers.

scenes.tts: In the Bay, the extra nutrients feed the algae. They grow very fast. A thick, fast growth of algae is an algae bloom. The green water shades underwater grasses. Then the algae die and sink to the bottom.
scenes.visual: algae multiply into a bloom, grasses shaded, algae turn grey and sink
scenes.narration: In the Bay, the extra nutrients feed the algae. They grow very fast. A thick, fast growth of algae is an algae bloom. The green water shades underwater grasses. Then the algae die and sink to the bottom.

scenes.tts: A decomposer is a living thing that breaks down dead matter. Bacteria decompose the dead algae. They use oxygen as they do. Dissolved oxygen is oxygen gas mixed into water. The deep water runs low on oxygen.
scenes.visual: bacteria on dead algae; oxygen dots leave the deep layer
scenes.narration: A decomposer is a living thing that breaks down dead matter. Bacteria decompose the dead algae. They use oxygen as they do. Dissolved oxygen is oxygen gas mixed into water. The deep water runs low on oxygen.

scenes.tts: In this lesson, a dead zone is water with less than two milligrams of oxygen per liter. It is not empty. Bacteria live there. The water may hold little to no oxygen. Why the deep water, and why summer? Warm water can hold less dissolved oxygen. In summer, fresher river water floats on saltier Bay water. The layers mix poorly, so new oxygen reaches the deep water slowly.
scenes.caption: In this lesson, a dead zone is water with less than 2 mg/L of oxygen. It is not empty. Bacteria live there. The water may hold little to no oxygen. Why the deep water, and why summer? Why the deep water, and why summer? Warm water can hold less dissolved oxygen. In summer, fresher river water floats on saltier Bay water. scenes.tts: Here is the chain. Extra nutrients feed an algae bloom. The algae die and sink. Decomposers use the oxygen in deep water that mixes poorly. Fish and crabs often swim away. Animals that cannot leave may get sick or die. Eutrophication is extra nutrients feeding too much algae growth. It can lead to low oxygen. So fertilizer does not take oxygen from the Bay by itself. Its nutrients feed algae. Decomposers use the oxygen.
